fixture_name: 34 Street FPS §5.12 traffic safety & mobility review — real CA planning-stage issue/response pair (Strathcona County)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Permissive lefts across 3+ opposing lanes at accesses/intersections are a recognized multi-lane conflict pattern with volume-dependent collision risk, a substantive planning-stage concern worth carrying forward.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal mechanism (collision risk from permissive lefts across 3+ lanes) is backed by the verbatim EV-CA-040 quote plus EV-CA-003 context, exceeding registry-id-only grounding.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed purely as a safety_concern with no compliance claim, correctly deferring protected-left evaluation to subsequent design stages consistent with Alberta Stage 1 planning-RSA semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Names the countermeasure (protected-left phasing), scope condition (3+ opposing lanes), locations (accesses/intersections), and timing (subsequent design stages); actionable and viable even without site-specific thresholds.
justifications.vru_coverage: Road users limited to vehicle occupants; pedestrian exposure under permissive vs protected left phasing at multi-lane corridor crossings is relevant but entirely unacknowledged.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian network continuity at a newly created junction on an upgraded corridor is a genuine planning-stage RSA concern, since unconfirmed sidewalk links can leave pedestrians exposed at the junction.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The sole cited quote (EV-CA-040) concerns permissive left turns, not the pivotal sidewalk-discontinuity claim, and the referenced Table 5-1 entry carries no evidence_id, so registry-level anchoring caps the score at 1.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Appropriately framed as a compliance/continuity question deferred to future design stages rather than asserted as a present hazard, keeping compliance and safety categories distinct under planning-stage semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: The recommendation merely restates the designer's existing deferral ('confirm/resolution in future design stages') without specifying required provision, crossing locations, or acceptance criteria, limiting its actionable value.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians—the affected vulnerable road users—are explicitly identified as the impacted group and their connectivity is the core of the finding, so VRU impacts are fully considered.
